improvements.title: Make TAMP a live environmental glitch detector: PVD + BOR pin + ADC4 analog watchdogs on VDD/VREFINT/temperature + GTZC2/TAMPSEC lock + tamp-irq in the ship set
improvements.threat: Voltage/clock/temperature fault injection on the U585 during the unlocked window (seed reconstructed in S-SRAM), RDP-2 -> RDP-1 downgrade glitches (Bozzato TCHES 2019 class; muGlitch had to defeat the L5 brown-out detector first), cold-boot SRAM retention, and a TAMP block whose RTC-domain security (GTZC2) is unconfigured so NS could in principle touch it.
improvements.proposal: (a) Arm PWR PVD at the level just below the pq1 operating point (Trezor: level 5 ~2.8 V) in rising+falling IRQ mode in BOTH the FSBL and the secure world, IRQ -> fi-barriered zeroize + reset (existing HardFault policy), and add PVD to the production fence so it cannot be omitted. (b) Pin BOR_LEV to the highest level compatible with the pq1 rail in the ship option-byte profile (`lockdown.rs` currently only READS BOR_LEV; `make stm32-harden-opts` is a bench recipe) and have Phase A verify it before the RDP burn. (c) Write an ADC4 driver that runs continuous conversions on VREFINT, VDD-sense and the internal temperature sensor with AWD1/2/3 thresholds, so ITAMP7/12/13 — already enabled in CR1 but inert because no ADC exists — become hardware-confirmed tampers (CR3=0) that erase backup registers and fire the existing tamp-wipe path without software in the loop; this also satisfies HARDENING.md 4.7 (refuse below ~0 C). (d) Configure and lock GTZC2 so TAMP/BKP-SRAM/RTC are secure-only (sau.rs:672-675 leaves it unconfigured on purpose today). (e) Add `tamp-irq` to RELEASE_FEATURES so shipping is IRQ-driven, not ~1 ms polled. (f) Resolve the ITAMP6 x BHK interaction (#208: CR3=0 erases BKP0R..7R holding the loaded BHK on any probe attach) before enabling ITAMP6 in confirmed mode, and run #391 (TAMP silicon test) as the acceptance gate.
improvements.rationale: The only brownout handling today is post-hoc reset-cause classification. Trezor arms PVD in boardloader, bootloader and kernel and pins BOR in option bytes; it enables the same ADC4 tampers but leaves them inert (no AWD configured anywhere in its tree), so (c) is a genuine step beyond both incumbents on the same silicon. ADC4 AWD -> ITAMP is the only STM32-native path from an analog measurement to a CPU-less secret erase, which is what the RP2350 and TROPIC01 results say software-only detection lacks. Items (d)-(f) are the missing delta of the partially-implemented TAMP port and are prerequisites for trusting (c).

improvements.title: Close the FSBL FI gate (EF-swarm F15): TRNG-fed wait_random, poisoned-default branch target, redundant WOTS-checksum verify, MSPLIM, and tripwire-mismatch escalation via a BKP mailbox
improvements.threat: Two coordinated faults with a single setup bypass the FSBL verify chain because every FSBL random delay is a constant; a faulted WOTS checksum during VERIFICATION accepts a forged image (Wagner et al. 2023, BSI LFI 2025); an option-byte tripwire that only halts leaves secrets and the downgraded unit intact for a second attempt; a silent FSBL stack overflow corrupts .data with no fault.
improvements.proposal: (1) Initialise the STM32U585 RNG in the FSBL (RCC enable + CR/HTCR/NSCR profile already in secure/src/hw/rng.rs, plus the zero/repeat software tests) and swap `rng_byte()` for a real read, so `wait_random` retimes every `check_true_into_sentinel`; (2) keep the slot entry address in a volatile that is poisoned (0 / non-executable) until the LAST gate of `filter_valid` + image verify passes, with a default `failed_jump` sink (Trezor `next_stage_addr` / `failed_jump_to_firmware`); (3) in the FSBL C10 verifier recompute the WOTS checksum / C10 target-sum twice with Hamming-distant results and compare before accepting; (4) program MSPLIM in `pre_init` of the FSBL (and secure + NS images; see SYS-03); (5) on a PERSISTENT option-byte mismatch write the verdict into a non-secret TAMP backup register / fixed SRAM mailbox and still halt — the secure world reads the mailbox at next boot and arms the page-125 wipe flag (the secure world already owns that write path), so a downgrade attempt costs the attacker the SE shares without giving the FSBL a flash writer. Budget: must stay inside 40,960 / 38,912 B LOAD span and 16 KiB stack (scripts/check_fsbl_geometry.py).
improvements.rationale: The FSBL is the one component invariant #10 makes unpatchable after RDP-2, so its FI posture must be final before freeze. Trezor's boardloader inserts a TRNG-randomised `fih_delay` before every `ensure()`, keeps the jump target zero until the end, and erases secrets on an option-byte mismatch; pq1's own fi.rs comment states the fixed-delay weakening explicitly. The BKP-mailbox escalation preserves the Draft 1.2 C1 rule (FSBL never writes option bytes) and the 'no runtime write path touches the FSBL range' rule while matching Trezor's wipe-on-mismatch outcome.

improvements.title: Memory-fault resilience: MSPLIM/PSPLIM in all three images, SRAM2/SRAM3 ECC with double-error NMI, flash ECCD NMI, and secret caches relocated to an ECC-on bank
improvements.threat: Silent stack overflow (C10 verify frames are ~10 KB) corrupting .data/secrets with no fault; laser/EM/Rowhammer-class bit flips in SRAM or flash reads (SLasH-DSA shows a memory fault during signing yields universal forgery; the ct-compare only catches faults that differ between passes) going undetected; the existing NMI handler has no source and the existing HardFault policy never triggers on a flipped bit.
improvements.proposal: (a) Set MSPLIM (and PSPLIM where PSP is used) in `pre_init` of secure, NS and FSBL so overflow raises UsageFault.STKOF -> escalated HardFault -> existing zeroize+reset; (b) enable SRAM2_ECC / SRAM3_ECC option bytes in the ship profile and RAMCFG ECC with ECC double-error -> NMI, single-error counters readable for telemetry; (c) place `SecureState` secret caches (master_secret, slot_master_entropy, SLOT_CACHE, OptRand/shuffle seeds, signing scratch) in the ECC-on bank via a dedicated linker section; (d) arm FLASH ECCD interrupt/NMI with the Trezor region-scoping rule (fatal always in the secure world; in the FSBL fatal only if the address is inside the FSBL's own range so a damaged slot does not brick the verifier); (e) close #374 with cargo-call-stack on the final production feature combination and make the FSBL frame-sum bound a CI gate.
improvements.rationale: Every one of these is a documented requirement (#48/#94/#542/#543/#374) with zero code since 2026-05. Trezor sets MSPLIM at reset, pins SRAM3 ECC in OPTR, decodes ECCD in the NMI handler, and clears unused stack at every stage. MSPLIM is a one-line, zero-cost detector that matters more for pq1 than a stack canary because the signing frames are large and Rust has no SSP by default. ECC turns the 'no software redundancy can see a flipped bit' class into a hardware fault that reuses the already-correct NMI/HardFault zeroize path.

improvements.title: Detected-fault escalation policy: an FI sentinel trip charges a PIN attempt, repeated trips lock and zeroize, SE alarm/reset retries are counted, and a persistent option-byte mismatch arms the wipe
improvements.threat: An attacker with the device characterises glitch parameters at zero cost: every ct_eq mismatch, CfiCounter desync, FihBool disagreement or SE link error today is a free retry (refusal only), and SE driver retries (up to 1000 reads / 500 WTX) silently mask repeated fault attempts; Trezor's bootloader treats a flipped secbool as 'most likely glitch' and erases storage.
improvements.proposal: Define and implement one escalation ladder in S-world: (1) any FI gate trip inside `c10_sign_verified*`, `gated_unlock`, `confirm()`/chord arming, `fw_update` verify, or `FihBool::is_true_fi` disagreement charges ONE page-124 attempt through the existing three-way precharge path (no new flash state) and records a reason code in `pin_attempt_log`; (2) a session glitch tally in SRAM: N trips (e.g. 3) -> lock + zeroize + reset; (3) SE drivers count resync/alarm/retry-exhaustion events per session and route >K to the same ladder instead of best-effort retry; (4) a persistent tz-1 mismatch (SYS-02 e) or ITAMP6 confirmed event arms the page-125 wipe flag, i.e. the existing `trigger_intrusion_wipe` policy extended to option-byte evidence; (5) keep HardFault/NMI as reset-only (owner rationale: single glitch must not brick) but count them via SYS-06 so a cluster of resets also feeds the tally. Bench builds keep the ladder log-only.
improvements.rationale: Hardware FI campaigns (Genêt ChipWhisperer 1024 queries at 1/3 fault rate; Donjon DS28C36 t-test-guided double fault) succeed by repetition. Charging the existing attempt counter is the cheapest way to make each attempt cost the attacker, uses only state the firmware already has, and respects 'no new per-signature flash state'. Trezor's shipped policy (secbool flip -> BHK regenerate + storage erase; option-byte mismatch -> secret_safety_erase) shows a vendor already treats detected faults as evidence, not noise.

improvements.title: Continuous timing desynchronisation: secure-TIM random-delay interrupt (RDI) with USB-refreshed session jitter, a DWT-CYCCNT instruction-timer canary around CfiCounter blocks, and random pre-delay + bounded waits in RCC/SAU setup
improvements.threat: Glitches timed from an external anchor (USB packet, TE pulse, LCD frame, SE I2C transaction) against the C10 sign, the double-sign compare, PIN entry, SAU/GTZC programming and the PLL bring-up (muGlitch faulted the L5 PLL config to get below the BOD), plus SCA trace alignment across the whole 6-14 s signing window rather than only the verify step.
improvements.proposal: (a) Port Trezor's RDI: a 1 ms secure-only timer (TIM2/TIM3 are already TZSC-secured) whose handler busy-waits `drbg8() + session_delay` cycles, with `session_delay` re-drawn on every USB RX/TX and every trusted-UI key event (floating-mean distribution), seeded from the platform TRNG and reseeded on a counter; (b) an instruction-timer canary: read DWT CYCCNT (or a secure TIM) at entry/exit of each CfiCounter-gated block (`c10_sign_verified` steps, `gated_unlock` precharge, SAU/GTZC/TZSC write sequence, fw_update verify) and treat an elapsed-cycle count outside a pre-measured [min,max] window as a fault (NXP CWT 'Instruction Timer' analogue) feeding SYS-04; (c) insert `wait_random()` before each SAU/GTZC/TZSC/RCC security write (read-back already exists) and bound the unbounded HSIRDY/HSI48RDY/PLL1RDY spins in rcc.rs with the same timeout pattern VOSRDY already uses; (d) fix #802 so `is_true_fi` does not do a full TRNG draw every SysTick after idle.
improvements.rationale: pq1 has stronger per-signature FI structure than Trezor but no continuous jitter; Trezor runs RDI in kernel and secmon and refreshes it from usb.c so a packet-aligned attacker still sees a per-session offset. muGlitch's countermeasure (random 0-9 cycle pre-delay) made two successful glitches ~100x less likely. The CWT instruction-timer idea is the hardware twin of the existing CfiCounter and catches clock-glitch / skip faults that leave the step counter intact.

improvements.title: Fault and tamper forensics with lockout-time persistence: capture CFSR/SFSR/SFAR/PC, TAMP SR, TZIC SR, reset cause and the PIN-attempt reason ring into a wipe-surviving public record and render the reason after the FSBL fingerprint
improvements.threat: A unit returned from the field (or #715 on the bench) cannot explain a lockout, a tamper trip or a cluster of resets; FI attempts are indistinguishable from flaky hardware; every diagnostic today is SRAM-only and destroyed by the very reset that the security response performs.
improvements.proposal: (1) On HardFault/NMI/TAMP/TZIC/PVD before `sys_reset`, snapshot the fault registers (CFSR, HFSR, SFSR, SFAR, BFAR, MMFAR, faulting PC, NS/S state), the TAMP/TZIC status words and the reset cause into non-secret TAMP backup registers that are NOT in the CR3-erased set (or a fixed secure-SRAM mailbox checked for a magic+CRC on next boot). (2) At the next boot, the secure world folds that snapshot plus monotonic counters (tamper events by source, fault resets, FI-sentinel trips, SE link resets, ECC single-error count) into a PUBLIC record class on page 127 written only on exceptional events (lockout, tamper, fault cluster) — the one-time flash write pin_attempt_log.rs already names as its follow-up — and persists the PIN-attempt reason ring at lockout. (3) The record survives the admin wipe (public class, Trezor backup_ram PUBLIC vs PROTECTED split) and is readable without PIN via a read-only CMD / shown as a short reason line after the FSBL fingerprint ('TAMPER: VOLTAGE' / 'PIN locked: 10 wrong' / 'FAULT x3').
improvements.rationale: Trezor records a first-fault postmortem (never overwritten), names the tamper source on RSOD, and persists monotonic min/max temperature + sticky error bits as a wipe-surviving public item; pq1 discards everything. Exceptional-event-only writes respect the 'no new per-signature flash state' rule. Field evidence is also what turns the SYS-04 ladder from a policy into something auditable.

improvements.title: Measure the whole slot windows, not only [base, base+len): include each slot's unused tail in the FSBL fingerprint so a payload parked in free flash changes the 8 words
improvements.threat: A stage-2 payload or implant-assisting stub written into the unused tail of the secure or NS slot (or into slack between images) is invisible to the boot fingerprint, because the FSBL hashes exactly the manifest-declared lengths; this is the 'firmware must not be compressible / spare flash must be unusable' assumption Donjon used to bypass Trezor Suite's firmware hash check on Safe 3, and the gap Krux closes by filling and hashing empty blocks.
improvements.proposal: Change `fsbl::verify::verify_images` to hash the FULL `SLOT_SECURE_CAPACITY` and `SLOT_NS_CAPACITY` windows (image bytes followed by the tail, which the signed manifest asserts is 0xFF — or a build-time deterministic fill the manifest commits to), and make `fw_update` COMMIT erase + verify the tail to that value; keep the fingerprint derivation `firmware_fingerprint_lines` over the window hash so the secure-world advisory row stays identical; extend `verify-ship-state` and the RDP-0 pre-power verifier to assert the same tails. Per-device pages 123-127 and the NS-slot atlas offset stay outside the measured window by design (they change at runtime / are separately pinned).
improvements.rationale: The FSBL fingerprint is the entire post-sale trust story (invariant #10 d); an unmeasured tail is free real estate for exactly the class of modification it exists to catch. Cost is hashing ~466,944 + NS-slot bytes instead of 385,568 + 7,488 (FSBL hashes at ~330 KB/s in software per verify.rs — roughly +0.3-0.5 s on a 6.9 s boot; with hw-sha256 much less).

improvements.title: RAM remanence hygiene: random-then-zero fill of all SRAM in the FSBL, wipe-all-but-stack before every stage handoff and before every reset/halt, clear unused stack, clear TAMP BKP registers, and pin SRAM2_RST
improvements.threat: Cold-boot / data-remanence recovery of a previous session's reconstructed entropy or slot SigningKey from SRAM (Donjon's 'unfixable' Trezor extraction class, RDP Freeze on STM32), and stale secrets surviving a FSBL->secure or secure->NS handoff or a reset that only zeroizes NAMED caches.
improvements.proposal: (1) In the FSBL reset path, after TRNG init (SYS-02), fill every SRAM region except the live stack with a TRNG word and then with 0 before .bss/.data init; (2) in the secure world, before branching to NS and inside the HardFault/NMI/panic/lock/idle-wipe paths, `memregion_fill` all runtime secure SRAM except the current stack via volatile stores (not memset), then clear the unused stack; (3) clear the TAMP backup registers that are not the BHK on handoff; (4) set SRAM2_RST=0 (SRAM2 erased on system reset) in the ship option-byte profile and verify it in Phase A; (5) pair with the SYS-01 temperature floor so a frozen-SRAM attack is refused at boot.
improvements.rationale: pq1 zeroizes named secret types and relies on .bss re-zero at startup; the 24-word entropy and C10 signing scratch (4008-B signatures, hypertree buffers) live on the stack and in temporaries that `ZeroizeOnDrop` covers only when destructors run — a fault, glitch or power cut skips them. Trezor's boardloader fills all RAM with random then zero, and every jump/reboot/halt wipes everything except the stack; the U585 SRAM2_RST option byte gives a hardware guarantee for the bank secrets can be placed in (SYS-03 c).

improvements.title: User-influenced entropy provenance: mandatory user-supplied entropy phase in the seed wizard (with visible effect), a two-run divergence test, and a documented or host-committed OptRand to bound the SPHINCS+ randomizer covert channel
improvements.threat: A backdoored or mis-configured TRNG, a factory-image RNG bug (Coldcard 2026: every test passed while seeds came from a 32-bit-bounded PRNG), or a malicious/implanted firmware that encodes key bits into the per-signature randomizer R / C10 grinding nonce (SPHINCS+ subliminal channel) — the one class the 3-source XOR does not address because all three sources are chosen by the device.
improvements.proposal: (a) Seed wizard: add a required entropy phase where the user enters >= 65 chord/arrow presses (or dice/coin values) that are hashed with the 3-source draw (`entropy = SHA256(rng_strong || user_bytes)`) and show the user that the FIRST word changes when they change one input, so a pre-programmed seed is impossible and the user can see their contribution; (b) add a host-side/QEMU differential test that two wizard runs with identical UID/SysTick/mock-SE inputs produce different seeds and that `rng_strong` output has >= 32 distinct bytes (Coldcard's `>4 distinct` check was vacuous), plus a KAT-style startup repetition test for the first SE responses (#641); (c) OptRand covert channel: either implement a host-commitment mode where the companion sends a nonce h and the device derives `opt_rand = SHA256("optrand-v1" || h || d)` with device nonce d returned alongside the signature (auditable later by a second device holding the same seed — not by the host alone, since R = PRF_msg(SK.prf, opt_rand, M) is unverifiable without SK.prf), or document explicitly in HARDENING.md that the R / target-sum-grind channel is an accepted residual against malicious firmware and that the FSBL fingerprint is the only defence; do not silently leave it unstated.
improvements.rationale: User-visible, user-manipulated entropy is the one defence that provably held across the 2026 Coldcard incident, and NGRAVE/Coldcard ship it; pq1's wizard takes none. Anti-exfil (Jade/BitBox02 anti-klepto) is the shipped answer to nonce covert channels on ECDSA; hash-based signatures have no host-verifiable analogue, so honesty plus a second-device audit path is the realistic 'beyond'. pq1's invariant #1/#4 story is strongest when the user can also rule out the device's own randomness as a single point of failure.
